analysis: The closest response uses close reading, art history, film interpretation, historical inquiry and social research to study cultural representation and public life. Research Methods and Statistics strengthens empirical methods alongside Qualitative Research Methodology. Renaissance art and the advanced art-history and historical seminars contribute well-defined inquiry through their official descriptions. The media plan adds programming, text and web data, AI ethics, television and digital representation to documentary work, media archaeology and critical interpretation. These are complementary digital humanities tools rather than a specialist film-production degree. The colonial histories and gender plan uses oral history, postcolonial theory, race and media, Indigenous historical inquiry, gender analysis and social movements. Politics and ethics provide institutional and interpretive context. All three are feasible and distinct; other coherent direction clusters remain at the three-option limit. Six pairings reflect actual shared methods or subject matter. Neither large external package is equated to a single UCR course. Where UCR overlaps through multiple courses or differs in method or scope, rows stay separate. The Utrecht internship and 7.5 EC thesis remain explicit. UCR independent research is an optional comparison element outside the schedule.

alignment.rationale: Both teach methods of literary interpretation. Utrecht’s course focuses on Dutch-language literature.
Both study talk and interaction. UCR includes turn-taking and dialogue within a broader stylistics course.
Utrecht connects literature, gender and media in one introductory course.
This course introduces language and communication in the Dutch language area.
Utrecht has a dedicated course in intercultural communication.
Utrecht studies how institutions manage linguistic diversity.
Both combine media analysis with collaborative production. UCR focuses on documentary.
Both study framing. Utrecht focuses on contested information and sources, while UCR applies persuasion to science communication.
Utrecht focuses specifically on identity in digital settings.
Both study how media represent cultural groups. UCR focuses on race, power and representation.
Both develop empirical research and statistical analysis. UCR applies these methods in a wider research context.
Utrecht develops humanities research through engagement with societal partners.
The internship counts toward Utrecht’s practical or international requirement.
Utrecht brings humanities theory, methods and professional reflection together in this course.
Utrecht develops the thesis proposal in a communication research lab.
Utrecht requires a thesis. UCR’s optional research element is outside the scheduled degree.
Students choose electives under Utrecht’s degree rules.
